architecture.summary: PR 2 of the habit-hooks cleanup stack changes the habit-hooks configuration only: .habit-hooks/config.toml and .habit-hooks/eslint.config.mjs. The line-count sensor gets a limit of 300 lines instead of 200 and skips test/ and the four WorkOS legal-text bundles, which hold data that a SHA-256 pins. no-unused-vars ignores a using declaration, because its binding exists for its dispose (src/index.ts). The five ESLint import-boundary blocks for src/auth, src/mcp, src/hosted-admin, src/page-fetch, and src/search-pipeline go: #214 removed those folders, so the blocks matched no file. The phase-one/import-context rule still applies the component graph of the rules file to each src file, and the dependency_graph of the PR checker guards the same boundaries at review. On all 1,415 tracked source files, ESLint gives the same messages with the old and the new configuration (120 and 119), except the using declaration in src/index.ts. The full scan has 1 oversized file instead of 87 (workos-organizations.ts, 448 lines, which PR 3 splits). The policy flag is set: the change relaxes what habit-hooks enforces. No production code, test, contract, dependency, composition, build output, or deployment relationship changes: nothing in src/, test/, the runtime images, or the workflows reads these files. The component registry describes the runtime system only; its prose and all 21 views remain accurate and unchanged.
